## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dukkhappahānavāyamapañha* ("The Question on Trying to Eliminate Sorrow", Mil 3.7.3) is a dialogue belonging to the *Milindapañha* section of late canonical and post-canonical Pali literature [SuttaCentral]. In modern translation, an English version has been prepared by John Kelly, alongside three other translations in two additional languages recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records a full parallel to the dialogue in the Chinese translation of the Milinda literature, T 1670b 2.63 (*Aim of Sramanahood*), as well as a passage-level doctrinal parallel in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 19.1, *Kilesajahanakathā*) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates substantial Pali-internal text reuse comprising 78 shared passages across eight Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal dialogue partners in the *Milindapañha* are the *Vāyāmakaraṇapañha* (Mil 3.4.5), *Bhavantasaṅkhārajāyamānapañha* (Mil 3.3.5), and *Purimakoṭipañha* (Mil 3.3.2), along with matches in the Vinaya commentary (*Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments also link passages of the text to Tibetan sutras—most prominently the *Rājadeśasūtra* (D0215) and the *Bimbisārapratyudgamana-mahāsūtra* (D0289)—and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
